req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The violation is that test[4] has kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is not valid for a negative kind test under the rule-based verifier. The fix is to change heuristic from STC to NEG for that test, which is the correct heuristic for a negative test verifying that a failed authorization attempt leaves system state unchanged. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were.

tests.name: test_author_can_delete_own_post
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=2 exists and is authored by user id=1 (Rahul)
Rahul is authenticated via POST /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-020: author deletes own post — success path
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

tests.name: test_non_author_delete_post_still_exists_after_403
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=7 authored by Anjali (user id=2)
Rahul (user id=1) is authenticated
actions: Verify post 7 still accessible via GET /7/update
expected: Post id=7 still exists after the failed delete (GET /7/update returns 200)
trace: R-FLASKR-020: negative state verification — post must remain in DB after rejected delete
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/7/delete')
assert r.status_code == 403
client.get('/auth/logout')
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.get('/7/update')
assert r.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_author_delete_then_non_author_gets_404_not_403
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=2 authored by Rahul (user id=1)
Rahul deletes post 2 first
Anjali (user id=2) then attempts to delete the now-missing post 2
expected: Second delete attempt returns 404 (post gone), not 403 — boundary between 403 and 404 error codes
trace: R-FLASKR-020: BVA boundary — 403 vs 404 depends on post existence; deleted post yields 404 not 403
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
client.get('/auth/logout')
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r.status_code == 404
assert r.status_code != 403
